title: R.S.M. Inter College And Bholarampur v. State of U.P. & Ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J.; Vivek Varma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; relegated to Clause 7.10 CGRF.
headnote: A writ challenging a distribution licensee's demand notice and a recovery citation for electricity dues is not maintainable under Article 226 where disputed questions of fact arise and an alternative remedy exists under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 of complaint to the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. The petition was disposed of with liberty to avail that forum.
facts: The petitioner, R.S.M. Inter College And Bholarampur, challenged a demand notice dated 1 February 2018 of the distribution licensee and a recovery citation dated 28 February 2020 for Rs 1,66,802 plus five talwana. It sought certiorari to quash both and mandamus against coercive recovery. Counsel for the Power Corporation respondents objected that Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provided an alternative remedy before the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. The petitioner did not dispute that remedy.

holding_units.topic: CGRF alternative remedy for demand and recovery disputes
holding_units.holding: Where a consumer's writ against a demand notice and recovery citation raises disputed questions of fact, the High Court will not entertain the petition under Article 226 and will relegate the petitioner to the alternative remedy of complaint before the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Applied to a challenge to a demand notice and recovery citation: billing/recovery grievance must take the Clause 7.10 forum route rather than a writ on disputed facts.
Clause 7.10 CGRF complaint treated as the available alternative remedy; petitioner did not dispute it, and the writ was disposed of with liberty to avail that forum.

not_decided.point: Validity of the demand notice dated 1.2.2018 and the recovery citation dated 28.2.2020
not_decided.note: Merits not examined because of disputed questions of fact and the Clause 7.10 alternative remedy.
